description: Generic IDTA template-cardinality knowledge behind the registry: what 'card.' means, which artefact the PDFs call definitive, and concrete JSON-vs-PDF cardinality divergences, each checked against the official template JSON or PDF text (never the derived registry files).

items.question: In an IDTA submodel template specification table, what does a cardinality ('card.') of 1 mean - that the element must be present once, or that it must hold a value?
items.expected_answer: It counts entries of the element: 1 means mandatory 1 entry (0..1 optional, 1..n mandatory 1 to many). The definition says nothing about the value having to be filled.

citation.section: Annex A. Explanations on used table formats, 2. Tables on Submodels and SubmodelElements
citation.quote: The table header abbreviates 'cardinality' with 'card'. The cardinality is defined with o 0…1: optional o 1: mandatory 1 entry o 1…n: mandatory 1 to many entries

items.question: Do IDTA submodel template PDFs say anything about whether their tables or the machine-readable template are the definitive definition?
items.expected_answer: Yes. The annex boilerplate says the tables do not convey all information and that the definitive definitions are given by a separate AASX file of the Submodel template.

citation.section: Annex A. Explanations on used table formats, 1. General
citation.quote: They do not convey all information on Submodels and SubmodelElements. For this purpose, the definitive definitions are given by a separate file in form of an AASX file of the Submodel template and its elements.

items.question: Which cardinality qualifier does the official AID 1.1 template JSON put on EndpointMetadata/contentType?
items.expected_answer: One (a Cardinality qualifier with value One), i.e. mandatory - stricter than the 1.1 PDF table, which prints 0..1.

citation.document: IDTA 02017-1-1 Asset Interfaces Description - official template JSON

items.question: The AID 1.1 template JSON marks EndpointMetadata/contentType as One. What cardinality does the AID 1.1 specification table give it?
items.expected_answer: 0..1 (optional): the PDF Table 4 and the JSON diverge on this element.

citation.section: 2.5, Table 4 Elements of SMC EndpointMetadata, row contentType
citation.quote: The local contentType definition (in the case it is used) overwrites this global contentType definition. [string] application/json 0..1

items.question: Does the AID 1.2 template JSON still mark EndpointMetadata/contentType as mandatory, as the 1.1 JSON did?
items.expected_answer: No. The 1.2 JSON carries an SMT/Cardinality qualifier with value ZeroToOne, matching the 0..1 of the specification table.

citation.document: IDTA 02017 Asset Interfaces Description - official template JSON

items.question: Is htv_methodName mandatory according to the official AID 1.1 template JSON?
items.expected_answer: No. The 1.1 JSON gives htv_methodName a Cardinality qualifier ZeroToOne, although the 1.1 PDF table prints 1.

citation.document: IDTA 02017-1-1 Asset Interfaces Description - official template JSON

items.question: The AID 1.1 template JSON makes htv_methodName ZeroToOne. What cardinality does the AID 1.1 specification table (Table 23) give it?
items.expected_answer: 1 (mandatory), so PDF and JSON diverge; the PDF is the stricter source here.

items.question: In AID 1.1 the template JSON gives oauth2_sc/flow the cardinality ZeroToOne. What does the specification table say?
items.expected_answer: Cardinality 1 (mandatory), e.g. value 'code'; JSON and PDF diverge.

items.question: The AID 1.1 specification table makes bacv_useService optional (0..1). Which cardinality does the official 1.1 template JSON give it?
items.expected_answer: One, i.e. mandatory - the JSON is stricter than the PDF table here.

items.question: In IDTA 02023 Carbon Footprint 1.0 the template JSON marks GoodsHandoverAddress ZeroToOne. What cardinality does the specification table give it?
items.expected_answer: 1 (mandatory) in the ProductCarbonFootprint table; JSON and PDF diverge.
